newsitem.title: USA: Boeing eyes higher production levels - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Boeing eyes higher production levels - WSJ.

text.p: Boeing Inc is getting ready to boost its production rate for all planes by 10 percent beyond the previously-announced levels, the Wall Street Journal said in Monday's electronic edition.
According to suppliers and people familiar with the situation, the company is examining how to double its output rate for the 737 aircraft, the newspaper said.

This would mean increasing 737 prodcution to 24 planes a month or more in the next two years and increasing production of its 747 jumbo jets by 25 percent, to five planes a month from four, the paper said.
The Journal also cited Boeing planning documents.
Boeing might aim to produce 28 to 31 of its 737 aircraft per month in 1999 and 2000, the paper said.
The company was not immediately available to comment.
